en: Homage to that Blessed One, the Worthy One, the Perfectly Self-Awakened One.
Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by a root, a state that is a root and accompanied by a root arises by way of root-condition.

Dependent on a state that is neither a root nor accompanied by a root, a state that is not a root but is accompanied by a root arises by way of root-condition. Dependent on a state that is neither a root...

Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor accompanied by root, there arise states that are both root and accompanied by root, and states that are neither-root and accompanied by root, by way of root-condition … three.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root and not accompanied by root, there arises a state that is neither-root and accompanied by root, by way of root-condition … one. (Abbreviated.

Under root-condition there are four; under object-condition there are four … pe … under prenascence and repetition there are three … pe … under resultant there are three … pe … under non-disappearance there are four.
A state that has multiple roots or no root is a condition, by way of root-condition, for a state that has no root or no root.
(Abbreviated. Under root: one; under object: six; under predominance: three; under proximity: six ... pe ...
under conascence and mutuality: four; under dependence: five; under strong-dependence: six; under prenascence: three; under repetition: one ... pe ... under association: [three].
One [condition], three in dissociation … pe … five in non-disappearance.
The Chapter on Questions (Pañhāvāra) should be expanded.
Dependent on a state that is neither-root nor rootless, a state that is neither-root nor rootless arises by way of the root condition … one.
Dependent on a state that is neither a root-cause nor rootless, there arises a state that is neither a root-cause nor rootless by way of root-condition … one.

Dependent on a state that is neither a root-cause nor rootless and a state that is neither a root-cause nor rootless, there arises a state that is neither a root-cause nor rootless by way of root-condition … one. (Abbreviated. Under root-condition there are three;
under object-condition, one … pe … under conascence-condition, five; under mutuality-condition, four … pe … under resultant-condition, three … pe … under non-disappearance-condition, five.
